channel.title: Said & Checked: AI and Technology — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about AI and Technology, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-25: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “I spoke to them, let me just put it that way. And I convinced them.” Unsettled. In the same interview Trump declined to say whom he spoke to ("I was represented at the board"). Nvidia's Nov. 23 release credits "input from senior levels of the United States government" without naming him, and no board member has confirmed or denied contact.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “He's apologized for that to the company, to the country and to his family and his wife, who's a fantastic person” Unsettled. Huang's Nov. 17 statement says he "deeply regret[s]" the problems he created for the board, owns his mistakes and tells his family "I love you"; it does not use the words apologize or sorry, and any private apology cannot be checked.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-24: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Donald Trump, Bill Huizenga)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “And we have done a very thorough investigation. And the investigation showed that he did -- I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong.” Unsettled. No federal agency or White House document reporting an investigation that cleared Huang was found; the only account is Trump's, who attributed it to Attorney General Todd Blanche's office. The Justice Department and Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed is open, and Nvidia's own board investigation is not federal and not finished.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: The president also revealed his extraordinary personal involvement in this, saying that he had called the board several times directly and indirectly, and spoke with Huang yesterday on the phone.” Unsettled. The call with Huang is confirmed: in the CNBC interview Trump said he called Huang "last night," Nov. 22. The board calls are not: he said he spoke to the board "directly and indirectly" and also "I didn't call 'em previously, actually. I called 'em a little bit through representatives," and gave no count.
  • Bill Huizenga, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “she was, and is, a spy” Unsettled. No U.S. government body was found to have officially identified Alice Huang as a spy, and none has said she is not one; the Nov. 16 Commerce and Justice Department statement describes an open criminal export-control investigation of Megaspeed and does not mention espionage. AskAmerica's screening-list data shows three Megaspeed companies (Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand) on the Commerce Entity List and no entry for her as an individual.

Disagreements

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Congratulations to NVIDIA on having made, what I consider to be, an absolutely GREAT decision!”
    Hakeem Jeffries, U.S. Representative from New York; House Democratic leader: “The decision by the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang is indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible.”
    Both statements in context
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “There's nothing wrong with a comeback, and they came back and they did the right thing. That was not an easy thing to do.”
    Hakeem Jeffries, U.S. Representative from New York; House Democratic leader: “The decision by the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang is indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible.”
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-23: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (John Kennedy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “that the Department of Commerce has allowed the Communist Party of China to circumvent our export controls on advanced chips” Unsettled. A Justice Department case shows at least $160 million of export-controlled Nvidia H100 and H200 chips were smuggled or attempted to China on falsified paperwork, and the Commerce Department's January 2026 rule moved H200-class licenses for China to case-by-case review. No inspector-general finding or Commerce record was found showing that Commerce permitted or failed to stop the smuggling, so whether it 'allowed' circumvention is not settled by the records.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Pete Ricketts)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Pete Ricketts, U.S. Senator: “the United States is a leader in developing this technology, and we have the advantage on high-end chips and high-end chip manufacturing.” Unsettled. A 2023 CRS report says U.S. firms lead in AI chip design and the U.S. leads in chipmaking equipment, but the most advanced AI chips are manufactured only by TSMC in Taiwan and Samsung in Korea.
  • Pete Ricketts, U.S. Senator: “in 2025, NVIDIA booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary.” Unsettled. Nvidia's fiscal 2026 annual report, which covers most of 2025, reports revenue by customer headquarters and gives no Singapore figure. The check found Singapore billings of $23.7 billion in the fiscal 2025 report, but that filing could not be read directly here, so the $104 billion figure is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
  • Pete Ricketts, U.S. Senator: “The Departments of State, War, Energy, Treasury, and the U.S. Trade Representative have also recommended that Megaspeed be added to the Entity List.” Unsettled. Treasury Secretary Bessent said Treasury, the Pentagon, State and USTR favored listing Megaspeed, as reported by The Next Web and CNBC; Energy was named only in a summarized report that was not read, so no source read names all five. Megaspeed has not been added to the Entity List.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Mike Lawler)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Mike Lawler, U.S. Representative from New York: “in the four major AI platforms, GAO was able to have them create a terrorist manifesto, if you will.” Unsettled. GAO report GAO-27-108814 (Nov. 18, 2026) says covert prompts got all four most-used generative AI platforms to produce feasible plans for mass-casualty attacks and attacks on the electrical grid after first refusing. The report does not use the word "manifesto"; whether attack plans count as the content described is a reading the evidence does not settle.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chuck Schumer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Forget explaining why his administration didn't reveal that a Chinese spy infiltrated one of America's leading companies.” Unsettled. The espionage claim rests on a New York Times report, carried by AP, that U.S. officials concluded the woman involved was a Chinese spy. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, Singapore authorities found insufficient evidence of a crime, and the FBI and board inquiries are open. No official finding of infiltration or of administration non-disclosure was found.

item.title: Said & Checked, AI and Technology, 2026-11-15: 1 false (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “And I chair the subcommittee that oversees the Department of Commerce that helped expose his involvement with the -- with Epstein.” False. The Senate Appropriations Committee's own page for its Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittee lists Jerry Moran as chair and Chris Van Hollen as ranking member, and AskAmerica's committee roster shows the same. Republicans hold the Senate majority until the new Congress is seated in January. The second part of the sentence, on what the subcommittee helped expose, was not checked: no page read addressed it.
